query: How do review facets differ by sentiment label?

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Punctuation intensity is a plausible facet that could vary by sentiment; values match source (AMZ-0003 has one '!'). Modestly useful, mostly zero-valued so limited leverage.

per_column.name: question_count
per_column.rationale: Rhetorical questions could differ by sentiment; counts match source (AMZ-0001 and AMZ-0003 each have questions). Heavily zero-skewed limiting differentiation.

per_column.name: caps_words_count
per_column.rationale: All-caps emphasis is a reasonable stylistic facet. AMZ-0003 'REAL' and AMZ-0005 'DVD' plausibly counted as 1; groundable, though intensity signal is weak.

per_column.name: avg_sentence_length
per_column.rationale: Sentence-length as a structural facet gives a genuine numeric axis to compare across sentiment; computed values look plausible for the sampled texts.

per_column.name: criticism_words_count
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to sentiment facets; lexicon counting is warranted (e.g. AMZ-0001 'disturbing/disappointed' -> 1). Some borderline cases (AMZ-0004 has 'negative' yet 0) suggest imperfect lexicon but generally grounded.

per_column.name: praise_words_count
per_column.rationale: Complements criticism count and is highly on-topic for facet-by-sentiment analysis; values mostly defensible though AMZ-0004's strong praise scoring 0 shows some undercount.

per_column.name: review_length_chars
per_column.rationale: Raw char length is a generic surface metric with weak analytical leverage. The 600 cap (many rows truncated) makes values only approximate for long reviews, slightly reducing groundedness.

judge.rationale: The added columns operationalize review 'facets' (punctuation intensity, caps emphasis, sentence structure, criticism/praise lexicon counts) that give real axes to compare across the sentiment label, directly serving the query; criticism/praise counts are the strongest, while raw char length is generic. Values are largely sound readings of the source text with no fabricated content; minor weaknesses are lexicon undercounts and a 600-char truncation cap that only approximates length for long reviews. No hallucinations observed.
